newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends lower, Central Bank buys dlrs.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends lower, Central Bank buys dlrs.

text.p: * Central Bank moves to prevent liquidity tightness
Late dollar buying by the Central Bank on Friday weakened the Philippine peso which closed at 26.222 pesos from 26.220, traders said.
The Central Bank's move was aimed at injecting more liquidity into the system to prevent tightness in the money market, traders said.
"Everybody's shifting to reverse repos. That may lead to a liquidity crunch," said a trader.

Banks find it attractive to invest in reverse repos since interest rates are now higher after the Central Bank raised its overnight borrowing rate by 2.25 percentage points to 12.50 percent this week to stop speculation on the peso, traders said.
They estimate the Central Bank bought about $16 million in late trading at 26.222 pesos.
The day's average, however, yielded a stronger peso at 26.218 to the dollar versus 26.222. Volume rose to $161.10 million from $111.70 million.
For most of the session, banks had been selling their dollars in exchange for pesos to take advantage of the interest premium on the peso.
Traders predict the Central Bank may start easing its overnight interest rates on Monday.
